To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
strain-induced ferrite formation can be induced in a strip-cast dual phase steel and it can be used for strengthening the steel.

strain-induced ferrite formation was observed in strip cast DP steel during thermo-mechanical processing, and that this ferrite formation led to an increase in strength with a slight reduction in ductility compared with polygonal ferrite.

strain-induced ferrite formation can be achieved during the thermo-mechanical processing using laboratory simulated strip caster, and the strain-induced ferrite is beneficial to the mechanical properties of dual phase steel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of deformation temperature on SIF formation and the effect of SIF on mechanical properties.
the development of DP steels using strip casting, and the effect of deformation on microstructure and mechanical properties of the resulting steels.
the microstructural evolution during deformation in the 700–800 °C temperature range and the effect of strain-induced ferrite on the mechanical properties of DP steels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SIF can be formed in a strip cast DP 700 steel and it can enhance the tensile strength of the steel.
the formation of SIF during thermo-mechanical processing can be used to enhance the mechanical properties of DP steels produced by strip casting.
the strain-induced ferrite formation in the strip cast DP steels is a promising route for the production of high strength DP steels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a DP steel produced via the strip casting route can be strengthened by deformation at 700–800 °C to form SIF, and the mechanical properties can be improved by increasing the amount of SIF in the microstructure.
the strip cast DP steels can be processed to achieve the mechanical properties of conventional DP steels, which are used in automotive industry.
the strip casting of DP steels is feasible, but the deformation conditions need to be optimized to produce the required microstructures and mechanical properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain DP steel with similar mechanical properties to those produced by conventional processing using the strip casting method.
the SIF formation is a promising route for the production of DP steels with enhanced strength and toughness via strip casting.
the SIF can be produced in a laboratory simulated strip casting and that the mechanical properties can be improved by the presence of the SIF.
